extraction.name: C-EVAL
extraction.description: C-EVAL is a comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite consisting of 13,948 multiple-choice exam questions spanning 52 diverse disciplines across four difficulty levels (middle school, high school, college, and professional), designed to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context.
extraction.creator: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from mock exams freely available on the internet, past exam questions from top universities in China shared by students, and mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam from the Weipu website. Manual annotation from PDF or Word documents was performed, followed by cross-validation. GPT-4 was used to generate explanation data, which was then manually revised.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Mock exams freely available on the internet, past exam questions from top Chinese universities shared publicly by students, and mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam from the Weipu website (approximately 2000 questions), sourced as PDF or Word documents.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Manual annotation from PDF or Word documents by a team of named annotators, followed by cross-validation of collected data. GPT-4-generated explanations were manually revised by team members.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Cross-validation of collected data by the annotation team.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Named team members: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Yikai Zhang, and Jiayi Lei (data collection and annotation); Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, and Junxian He (explanation revision).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used to generate explanation data.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark may have biases as it does not cover safety, bias, and robustness aspects of LLM evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: C-EVAL is limited to Chinese-context evaluation and does not cover all LLM abilities such as API reasoning, safety, bias, and robustness. It is also limited to accuracy-based evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to guide developers in preparing LLMs for complex scenarios in a Chinese context, potentially improving AI capabilities for Chinese-language users.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluating large language models (LLMs), particularly in a Chinese context, covering a wide range of subjects and difficulty levels including professional certifications, high school, and college-level knowledge.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions with fewer than four options are eliminated; for questions with more than four options, incorrect choices are randomly dropped to standardize to exactly four choices. Data is randomly split into development (5 exemplars per subject), validation, and test sets with a 1:9 ratio. Few-shot chain-of-thought explanations are generated by combining GPT-4 automatic generation and human annotation for the development split.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF documents are processed into text. Questions are parsed automatically or manually into a structured format. Complex mathematical notations are manually converted into standard LaTeX format. All questions go through deduplication and cleaning. Questions undergo multiple rounds of human validation, and all LaTeX notations are checked for syntax errors.

name.evidence: We present C-EVAL, the first comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite designed to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context.

description.evidence: C-EVAL consists of 13948 multiple-choice exam questions spanning 52 diverse disciplines, ranging from humanities to science and engineering... The questions are collected from four difficulty levels: middle school, high school, college, and professional tests.

url.evidence: The C-EVAL data and evaluation code are available at https://github.com/hkust-nlp/ceval.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The primary source of our data is mock exams freely available on the internet. In addition, a portion of the college-level questions are past exam questions from top universities in China, publicly shared by the students. A minor fraction of college questions are mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam, sourced from the Weipu website – these questions are not freely available to the public, and we have obtained their authorization to include around 2000 such questions into C-EVAL.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: There are many other abilities such as reasoning over and calling APIs, as well as multiple aspects that extend beyond accuracy, including safety, bias, and robustness.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We also note that, C-EVAL, along with all the English-language benchmarks, is far from perfect for LLM evaluation. There are many other abilities such as reasoning over and calling APIs, as well as multiple aspects that extend beyond accuracy, including safety, bias, and robustness.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: We believe that the evaluation of LLMs should transcend the scope of casual conversational bots, guiding developers in preparing LLMs to function in more complex scenarios. This was the primary motivation behind the creation of C-EVAL, a challenging evaluation suite.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We believe that the evaluation of LLMs should transcend the scope of casual conversational bots, guiding developers in preparing LLMs to function in more complex scenarios. This was the primary motivation behind the creation of C-EVAL, a challenging evaluation suite. We hope that C-EVAL along with C-EVAL HARD have made important progress on this direction particularly in a Chinese context.
